original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: F2[GL2(F2)] rank-one-idempotent register model with free scalar GL4(F2) mixing: four coordinate-SWAP targets diag([S],[S],[S],[S]), S = aba = bab, at exactly four registers with arbitrary dirty inputs fully restored. Exact paid-call minimum q; complete exclusion of q in {2,4,6}, parity L1 leaves q in {8,10} below the 12-call upper bound. Validation reproduces the t=1,2,3 minima 3, 6, 6, 9 in the same engine.
scope_change_reason: Refinement inside the card's allowed variation (fixed larger register count, specified nonabelian family): target count t = 4 is the boundary the coordinate-CNOT line's own statements leave open (PR1541 body: 'Four or more targets remain open'; PR1414 is t=2 at any workspace, PR1491 t=3 at exactly three registers, PR1541 t=3 at any workspace). This is not the excluded three-register abelian model.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the nonbinding bit side: no paid profile, supplier or moment changes. It prices an explicit nonabelian register alphabet's SWAP-target tariffs, one input to whether any small-width completed saving could change the bit primitive; a q < 12 word would have been such a mechanism, and its absence at q <= 6 narrows where one could live.
stop_rule: Kill the exact search when the required ball exceeds the host budget (depth-4 ball at r = 4 measured at about 2.7e8 to 3.4e8 states by bitmap sketch), record the measured growth and the residual domain q in {8,10}, and hand off rather than lower the target.
evidence: RECEIPT.json (ball sizes 240 / 32,651 / 3,639,920 at depths 1-3, all meets nat_hits=0 for q = 2,4,6 and for the validation cases, 12-call attaining word verified exactly in M_4(F2[G]) with a drop-one-call mutation control, 252 natural-image alias pairs with unequal formal values, engine-B cross-check on every ball through r=3 depth 4). Final line: PASS_FOUR_SWAP_R4_CNOT validation t2r2_min=6 t2r3_min=6 t3r3_min=9 t4r4 excluded={2,4,6} residual={8,10} upper=12.
author: Aaron Wang

open_questions.question: Do four coordinate-SWAP targets at r = 4 need 12 calls, or can a 10- or 8-call word reach diag([S],[S],[S],[S])? Parity L1 leaves exactly q in {8,10}.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It completes the first open target count of the coordinate-CNOT line and decides whether the 3-calls-per-SWAP tariff holds at t = 4.
open_questions.first_step: Run the 4+4 natural-image meet at the measured depth-4 ball (about 2.7e8-3.4e8 states) with 4-8 on-disk or sharded passes and formal-algebra resolution of any hit; if empty, the same for 5+5 or a written J^2/J^3 coefficient-layer bound for q = 10.
open_questions.blocked_by: Ball size: one exact depth-4 ball is about 3e8 64-bit states (roughly 20 GB in a CPython set), and the 5+5 meet needs its depth-5 successor; no SAT or C++ tooling is installed in this session by policy.
